ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ الْمَلِكِ الْقُدُّوسِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ (١))
His saying (الْمَلِكِ): it and what follows it are read in the genitive as naʿt (adjective), and in the nominative as a new beginning (istiʾnāf). The majority read the qāf of «الْقُدُّوسِ» with ḍamma, and it has been read with fatḥa; they are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا رَأَوْا تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْوًا انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْهَا وَتَرَكُوكَ قَائِمًا. . . (١١))
His saying (إِلَيْهَا): the pronoun was made feminine only because He referred it back to the merchandise (التِّجَارَة), since that was more important to them. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَآخَرِينَ مِنْهُمْ لَمَّا يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (٣))
His saying (وَآخَرِينَ): it is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to الْأُمِّيِّين.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ حُمِّلُوا التَّوْرَاةَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوهَا كَمَثَلِ الْحِمَارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفَارًا بِئْسَ مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ (٥))
His saying (يَحْمِلُ): it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْحِمَارِ», and what governs it is the meaning of الْمَثَل (likeness).
His saying (بِئْسَ مَثَلُ): this «مَثَلُ» is the fāʿil (agent) of بِئْسَ. On «الَّذِينَ» there are two views.
The first: it is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الْقَوْم, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "this likeness". The second: it is in the position of the nominative, its implied form being "evil is the likeness of the people: the likeness of those who…"; so the omitted مَثَل is the one specified for blame; it was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ إِنَّ الْمَوْتَ الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مُلَاقِيكُمْ. . . (٨))
His saying (فَإِنَّهُ مُلَاقِيكُمْ): the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ, and the fāʾ entered because of the resemblance of «الَّذِي» to a condition. Some disallowed this, saying: this is permissible only when الَّذِي is the mubtadaʾ (subject) or the noun of إِنَّ, whereas الَّذِي here is an adjective (ṣifa). They also weakened it from another angle, namely that fleeing from death does not save from it, so it does not resemble a condition; these people said: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida).
This has been answered: the adjective and the described noun are like a single thing; and since «الَّذِي» can only be an adjective, when the described noun is not mentioned with it the fāʾ enters while the described noun is intended, so it is likewise when it is stated explicitly. As for what they mentioned second, it is not correct, for a great many people think that fleeing from the causes of death will save them until another time.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَاةِ مِنْ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فَاسْعَوْا إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (٩))
His saying (مِنْ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ): «مِنْ» is in the sense of فِي (on). And الْجُمُعَة, with two ḍammas and with the mīm vowelless [الْجُمْعَة], is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of الِاجْتِمَاع (gathering). It is also said of the form with the vowelless mīm: it is in the sense of "that in which people gather", like رَجُلٌ ضُحْكَةٌ, i.e. one who is laughed at.
It is also read with fatḥa on the mīm [الْجُمَعَة], in the sense of the active participle, i.e. "the day of the place that gathers", like رَجُلٌ ضُحَكَةٌ, i.e. one who laughs a lot.
«[Translator's note: the source has «فِي الْمَسْكَنِ» ("in the dwelling"), evidently a corruption of «فِي الْمُسَكَّنِ» ("of the vowelless form"); translated in the latter sense.]»
